title: Ethics dilemma
description:
You walk past a colleague's desk and see their SSO password on a sticky note. What do you do?

Respond in 200+ words citing at least two ISC2 Code of Ethics canons by number and by the specific obligation each one imposes. The canons read, in order: (I) Protect society, the common good, necessary public trust and confidence, and the infrastructure. (II) Act honorably, honestly, justly, responsibly, and legally. (III) Provide diligent and competent service to principals. (IV) Advance and protect the profession.

Your response must address:

1. The immediate action you take in the moment — and why that order. What gets touched first, what waits.
2. Who you inform, and through which channel (in-person, ticket, manager). Justify the channel choice.
3. How you help the colleague without shaming them. Name the specific cultural risk of getting this wrong — people start hiding mistakes instead of surfacing them, and the next sticky note never makes it into a ticket.
4. Cite the two canons by number and quote the obligation language. Paraphrasing the canon as your citation does not count.

Reference: ISC2 Code of Ethics (https://www.isc2.org/Ethics).

Amaka grades this personally.

---

**Universal grading rule.** Generic answers fail. Every claim in your submission must be tied to specific evidence — an artefact from the lab (file path, log line, command output, payload, screenshot) **and** at least one external citation where research is relevant (NIST section number, MITRE technique ID, CVE, vendor advisory, ISO control ID, GDPR article). Claims without an attached artefact, timestamp, payload, standard section, or business constraint earn zero for that claim. Lab-only answers earn partial credit. External-only answers earn partial credit. Full credit requires both.
